docs.title: Usage limits
docs.text:
Pro is not unlimited.

  • Usage is counted over a five-hour session. When you reach the limit, Claude shows when it resets.
  • There is also a weekly limit on top of the session limit.
  • Chat, longer tasks, Claude Code and the desktop app all share the same allowance.
  • Long conversations, large files, long multi-step tasks, Opus and a high effort setting use the allowance faster.
  • Check where you stand in Settings → Usage.
  • Usage credits: you can switch them on so that work continues, at a cost, when you hit the limit. Leave them off if you don't want to pay more than the subscription. Fable always uses them.

To make it last: start a new chat for each new topic, put files you reuse in a Project instead of re-uploading them, and keep Opus and high effort for the problems that need them.

If you regularly hit the limits, the Max plan offers 5× or 20× more usage at a higher price.

docs.title: What Pro does not include
docs.text:
• No contract between UB and Anthropic. Pro is a personal (consumer) plan. Your data is handled under Anthropic's consumer terms, not an institutional agreement. Read Data and privacy.
  • No API access. Using Claude from your own programs through the API is billed separately at platform.claude.com. (Max and Team plans now include some monthly API credits; Pro does not.)
  • No shared admin. Projects and chats are yours; you cannot share a Project with colleagues. There is no ICCUB-wide workspace. A group Team plan adds sharing.

docs.title: Tips and pitfalls
docs.text: The most common traps, and how to avoid them. Most of them come down to one rule: Claude is a fast, knowledgeable assistant that is sometimes confidently wrong. You remain responsible for what you use.

docs.title: References and citations
docs.text:
Claude can invent references that look real (plausible authors, journal, year) or attribute a claim to the wrong paper.

  • Check every reference on ADS or arXiv before using it.
  • Ask "Which of these references are you certain exist?", and treat "not certain" as "probably invented".
  • With web search or Research on, Claude cites real pages, but check that the page says what Claude claims.

docs.title: Numbers, derivations and units
docs.text:
• Re-derive key steps yourself. Errors hide in factors of 2, π, signs, and h conventions.
  • Ask for units at every step and a sanity check (order of magnitude, a known limit).
  • For data analysis, ask for the code that produced a number and run it yourself.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Run it. Test it on a case where you know the answer.
  • Read diffs before accepting changes in Claude Code or VS Code.
  • Watch for code that "works" by quietly skipping data, catching all exceptions, or hard-coding a result.

docs.title: Claims about your own data or code
docs.text: Claude can describe your file or code with great confidence and be wrong, especially for long files. Ask it to quote the line or cell it is talking about.

docs.title: Getting better results
docs.text:
• Give context: who you are, who it is for, what good looks like. See Chat and prompting.
  • Iterate in the same chat, but start a new chat when you change topic.
  • Ask for a plan first for anything big: an outline before a paper, a plan before refactoring.
  • Work in small steps: one section, one function, one chapter at a time.
  • Get a second opinion: paste the answer into a new chat and ask for an independent check.
  • Use Projects and CLAUDE.md to avoid repeating instructions. See Projects.

docs.title: Data, privacy and safety
docs.text:
• Don't upload referee reports, proposals you are evaluating, student data with names, or passwords. See Data and privacy.
  • With connectors, Claude in Chrome and longer tasks, Claude acts as you. Ask for drafts, use the Manual permission setting for anything sensitive, and approve actions yourself.
  • Memory carries context from one chat to the next. Turn it off for confidential work (see Data and privacy).
  • Text in emails, web pages or documents can contain instructions aimed at AI ("prompt injection"). Don't let Claude act on instructions it found inside content.

docs.title: Acknowledging AI use
docs.text:
• Papers: most journals (A&A, MNRAS, ApJ, Physical Review…) ask you to declare how AI tools were used, usually in the acknowledgements or methods. AI cannot be an author. Check your journal's current policy.
  • Collaborations: many have their own rules on AI and on sharing internal material. Check before using Claude on collaboration documents.
  • Teaching material: say when notes or exercises were prepared with AI assistance.
  • Students: tell them clearly what AI use is allowed in your course, and assume they use it for take-home work.

docs.title: Usage limits
docs.text:
• Long chats, large files, long tasks, Opus and a high effort setting use your allowance faster.
  • Fable is not included in Pro: it is paid with usage credits. Check the model picker before a long session.
  • Put files you reuse in a Project instead of re-uploading them.
  • If you hit the limit, the reset time is shown. See What Claude Pro includes.

docs.title: Common surprises
docs.text:
Surprise Why What to do Claude doesn't know about a recent paper or software version Its knowledge stops at a training cut-off Ask it to search the web, or upload the paper Claude brings up something from another chat Memory is on Edit or delete that memory topic, or turn memory off for the chat The menus don't match this guide Anthropic is rolling out a new layout gradually Look for the same name nearby; the guide gives both names where they differ It forgot something from the start of a long chat Long chats are summarised or drop detail Start a new chat with a short summary of what matters It agrees with everything you say It tends to accommodate the user Ask it to argue against your idea, or to find the weakest point The same question gives different answers Answers are not deterministic Ask for reasoning, compare, and check It refuses something harmless Over-cautious safety filters Rephrase with context: who you are and why you need it

Have a pitfall to add? Tell us.

docs.title: How to use Claude
docs.text:
One page per feature. Each page says what the feature is, when to use it, and how, with ICCUB examples.

Page Read it when you want to… Chat and prompting get better answers from an ordinary chat Uploading files work with papers, data, plots or code Projects keep files and instructions together for a course, a paper or a proposal Artifacts get a document, a slide deck, a design, a quiz or a small app you can edit, export and share Longer tasks and scheduling hand Claude a whole task, let it work on files on your computer, repeat it on a schedule, or teach it with skills Web search and Research have Claude look things up and cite its sources Connectors let Claude read your Google Drive, email, calendar or GitHub Email, calendar and documents let Claude help with your inbox, meetings and admin Claude in Chrome let Claude read and act on web pages in your browser Claude Code have Claude read, edit and run code in your own projects Claude in VS Code use Claude inside VS Code for code, LaTeX and notes Claude Science run research analyses with provenance and your own compute (beta)

If you are new, start with Chat and prompting. Everything else builds on it.

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text: When Claude produces something substantial (a document, a slide deck, a design, a small interactive page), it opens it in a panel next to the chat. That is an Artifact. All your Artifacts are kept in the Artifacts tab of the left sidebar.

docs.title: Kinds of Artifact
docs.text:
Since September 2026, Artifacts come in a few types. You don't need to pick one: ask for what you want and Claude chooses. You can also start from a template in the Artifacts tab.

Type Good for Export to Docs A course handout, a one-page project summary, a report, meeting notes Word, PDF, Markdown, Google Docs Slides A talk, a seminar, lecture slides from your notes PowerPoint, PDF, Google Slides Design A poster, a one-pager, a landing page for an event, a mock-up PDF, PowerPoint, HTML, .zip Dashboards (beta) Live charts from data in a connected app Interactive pages A slider that shows how a Planck spectrum changes with temperature, a quiz for students, a simple calculator

Artifacts made before September 2026 still work and can still be published, but new ones use the types above.

docs.title: Working with them
docs.text:
• Change it by asking: "Add a second slider for redshift", "Make slide 4 less crowded."
  • Edit it yourself: type directly in a doc, edit any slide, or move elements on a design.
  • Edit one part with Claude: select text in a doc and click Edit with Claude, then say what to change. Claude only touches that part.
  • Present slides directly from Claude with Present, or download them.
  • Go back: editing an earlier message in the chat starts a new branch with its own Artifacts, so the original stays intact.

If Artifacts don't appear, check that Create and edit files (formerly Code execution and file creation) is on in Settings → Capabilities.

docs.title: Sharing
docs.text:
• New Artifacts are private to you until you share them.
  • Share gives you a link. Check who can open it before you send it, and don't share anything you would not put on a public web page.
  • Older Artifacts (before September 2026) must be published to share them; anyone with the link can see and use them without an account.
  • Some interactive Artifacts store data. If an Artifact uses shared storage, everyone who opens it sees what is entered. Don't type sensitive data into one.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Slides for a seminar

"From the attached paper, make 12 slides for a 30-minute ICCUB seminar: motivation, method, three key results with the figures from the paper, and an outlook slide. Use a plain white style with large fonts."

An interactive plot for a class

"Make an interactive page with a slider for the temperature of a black body from 3 K to 30 000 K. Show the Planck spectrum on a log-log plot, mark the Wien peak, and print the peak wavelength. Add a toggle for wavelength vs frequency."

A quiz

"Make a 10-question multiple-choice quiz on stellar evolution for first-year students. Show the right answer and a one-line explanation after each answer. Show a score at the end."

A one-page summary

"Turn the attached proposal into a one-page summary doc for the ICCUB website, with a title, three short paragraphs and a 'Key numbers' box. Export it as Word."

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Interactive Artifacts run in the browser. They are not a replacement for real analysis code.
  • Check physics and numbers in an Artifact just as you would in a chat answer: a nice-looking slide or slider can still use the wrong formula.
  • Exported PowerPoint or Word files may need layout fixes; open them before you present or send them.

Reference: What are artifacts and how do I use them? (Anthropic help center).

docs.title: Claude in Chrome
docs.text: Claude in Chrome is a browser extension that lets Claude read, click and type in web pages, in a side panel next to the page. It can do multi-step tasks on websites for you: fill a form, collect information across several tabs, navigate an awkward web portal. It is included in Pro, for Google Chrome on desktop only (not other Chromium browsers, not mobile).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. In Google Chrome (desktop), go to the Chrome Web Store and search for Claude by Anthropic.
  2. Click Add to Chrome.
  3. Sign in with your Claude Pro account.
  4. Pin it: click the puzzle icon in the toolbar, then the pin next to Claude.
  5. Click the Claude icon to open the side panel.

What changed in autumn 2026

  • The side panel is becoming a full Claude session (it was called a Cowork session): your conversations are saved, sync with your other devices, and can use your skills and connectors. This reaches Pro accounts gradually. To go back, click the three dots at the top right of the panel and choose Switch back to classic.
  • Scheduled tasks: the clock icon at the top right of the panel runs a browser task daily, weekly or monthly.
  • Shortcuts: save a prompt you reuse and call it by typing /.
  • The desktop app now has its own built-in browser, which Claude can use instead of Chrome during longer tasks. Choose which one in Settings → Cowork → Preferred browser. To let the desktop app use Chrome, go to Customize → Connectors, click Configure next to Claude in Chrome and switch it on.

docs.title: What it is good for
docs.text:
• Collecting information: "Open the registration pages of these three conferences and make a table with dates, fees, abstract deadline and early-bird deadline."
  • Tedious portals: "Go through the steps on this page to download the observing log for proposal 2026A-017." (you stay logged in yourself)
  • Reading what you are looking at: "Summarise this paper's abstract page and tell me if they use the same simulation suite as us."
  • Forms: "Fill in this travel form with the details from the confirmation email I opened in the other tab. Don't submit."

docs.title: Safety first
docs.text:
Claude in Chrome acts as you, in sites where you are logged in. Treat it like giving someone your laptop for a few minutes.

  • Check the permission mode. The side panel starts in Automatically approve, where Claude only stops when an action needs approval. While you learn, switch to a mode that asks before each action; the panel remembers your choice.
  • Start with read-only tasks. Let it collect and summarise before you let it type or click Submit.
  • Ask it to stop before submitting: add "Don't submit, I'll check first" to any form task.
  • Site permissions: Claude asks before acting on a new site. Only allow sites you need. Avoid banking, UB payroll and HR portals.
  • Untrusted pages can contain hidden instructions aimed at AI assistants ("prompt injection"). Don't let Claude act on pages you don't trust, and watch what it does.
  • Everything Claude reads on a page becomes part of your chat. See Data and privacy.

docs.title: Chrome extension or connectors?
docs.text:
If a service has a connector (Gmail, Google Drive, Google Calendar, GitHub…), use the connector: it is faster and more reliable. Use Chrome for websites that have no connector, such as conference sites, journal submission systems or university portals.

Reference: Getting started with Claude in Chrome (Anthropic help center).

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
Claude Code is Claude working directly on your computer, inside a code folder. It reads your files, edits them, runs commands and tests, and uses git. It is included in Pro and shares the same usage allowance as chat.

Use it instead of the chat when the task is about your own code: a pipeline, an analysis repository, a simulation, a LaTeX paper.

docs.title: Where to run it
docs.text:
• Terminal (macOS, Linux, Windows): the full version. Instructions below.
  • VS Code and JetBrains: install the Claude Code extension. It shows changes as diffs in the editor. See Claude in VS Code.
  • Desktop app: open the Code tab. No separate install; you see diffs visually, run several sessions side by side and can schedule recurring tasks.
  • Web (claude.ai/code) and the mobile app: no install. These work on a GitHub repository in the cloud, not on your laptop, and keep running when you close the page.
  • Remote Control: start a session on your own machine, then follow and steer it from your phone or another browser.

docs.title: Install (terminal)
docs.text:
macOS, Linux or WSL:

curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

Windows PowerShell:

irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

Or with Homebrew (brew install --cask claude-code) or WinGet (winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode); these two don't update automatically. Check it worked with claude --version in a new terminal window.

Then go to a project folder and start it:

cd ~/work/my-analysis
claude

The first time, it opens your browser to log in. Choose your Claude Pro account.

Full and up-to-date instructions: Claude Code quickstart.

docs.title: Good first tasks
docs.text:
Start by letting it read before it writes:

  • "What does this project do? Explain the folder structure."
  • "Where is the redshift-space distortion computed, and what are its inputs?"

Then small, checkable changes:

  • "Write tests for cosmology.py, then run them."
  • "This script crashes with the attached error. Find and fix the cause."
  • "Convert this Fortran 77 routine to Python with numpy, and check both give the same output on the test file."
  • "Fix the LaTeX warnings in paper.tex and make the reference style consistent."
  • "Review my uncommitted changes and point out bugs."

docs.title: Stay in control
docs.text:
• Use git. Commit before asking for big changes, so you can always go back. Ask Claude to "show me what you changed" before you commit.
  • Permissions. On Pro, Claude Code now starts in Auto mode: a safety classifier reviews most actions instead of asking you. Press Shift+Tab to switch mode, for example to Manual (asks before every change) while you learn, or to plan mode to get a plan before anything is touched. Typing /plan followed by a task does the same.
  • Don't run it on folders with secrets or data you cannot share (see Data and privacy). It reads what it needs from the folder you start it in.
  • Check the results: run the tests and look at the plots. Claude Code can be confidently wrong about scientific details.

docs.title: Make it know your project
docs.text:
Create a file called CLAUDE.md at the top of your repository. Claude Code reads it at the start of every session. Put in it what a new student would need to know:

# Project notes for Claude
- Python 3.11, numpy/scipy/astropy. Run tests with `pytest tests/`.
- Units: distances in Mpc/h, masses in Msun/h.
- Never modify files in `data/raw/`.
- The main pipeline entry point is `run_pipeline.py`.

Type /init in Claude Code to have it draft one for you. Claude Code also keeps its own auto memory of what it learns about the project between sessions.

docs.title: Go further
docs.text:
• Skills: type / to see the commands and skills available. You can write your own (for example, "how we produce paper figures") and Claude Code uses them when relevant. See Skills.
  • Scheduled tasks: /schedule creates a task that runs in the cloud on a schedule, such as a nightly test run or a weekly dependency check.
  • One-off commands: claude -p "explain this function" answers and exits, so you can use Claude in scripts.
  • Connect tools with MCP servers, for example to read issues from GitLab or tickets from a tracker.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Command What it does claude Start a session in the current folder claude -c Continue the last session in this folder claude -r Pick an earlier session to resume /clear Start a fresh conversation (use it when you change task) /help List commands Shift+Tab Switch permission mode Esc Interrupt Claude

To learn more, the free Claude Code 101 course is a good next step.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text: Connectors let Claude read from (and sometimes act in) other services you use: Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, Microsoft 365, GitHub, Notion and others.

docs.title: When they help
docs.text:
• "Find the latest version of the ERC proposal in my Drive and list what is still missing."
  • "What meetings do I have next week, and which clash with my teaching?"
  • "Summarise the open issues in our pipeline's GitHub repository."
  • "Find the email from the journal about my revision deadline."

Without connectors you would download and upload each file yourself.

docs.title: Connect a service
docs.text:
1. Open Customize → Connectors (in the left sidebar, or at claude.ai/customize/connectors). You can also click + in a chat and hover over Connectors.
  2. Find the service and click Connect.
  3. Sign in to that service and approve the access it asks for.

Use your UB account for UB Google or Microsoft services, so Claude sees work files and not personal ones (or the reverse, if that is what you want).

In a chat, open + to switch individual connectors on or off. Leave on only the ones that chat needs.

docs.title: What Claude can see
docs.text:
• Claude can access what your account can access in that service, but only reads what is relevant to your request.
  • What it reads becomes part of that chat, under the same rules as a file you upload. See Data and privacy.
  • Many connectors can also act: create a calendar event, draft or send an email, edit a Google Doc or Sheet. Claude asks for your confirmation before sending, sharing or deleting. Read the confirmation before you approve.
  • Connectors also work while Claude does a longer task or a scheduled one, so a scheduled task can read your email every Monday.

Warning

Connecting your UB email or Drive gives Claude access to whatever is in there, including other people's data. Point it at specific files or folders, and disconnect services you no longer use (Customize → Connectors → Disconnect).

docs.title: More
docs.text:
• Email, calendar and documents: Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Google Docs and Sheets, and Microsoft 365 in detail.
  • Plugins bundle connectors with ready-made skills for a type of work; browse them in Customize. See Skills.
  • Claude in Chrome: for websites that have no connector.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Be specific about where to look: "in the folder 'Teaching 2026'" is faster and safer than "in my Drive".
  • Combine with Research: Claude can search the web and your Drive in the same investigation.
  • For GitHub, the connector lets Claude read repositories. To have Claude change code, use Claude Code.

docs.title: Email, calendar and documents
docs.text: With connectors, Claude can search your email, read attachments in your Drive, check your calendar and draft replies. This is the most useful set-up for admin work: travel, reimbursements, meeting planning, reports.

docs.title: Which connector
docs.text:
Your account Connector What Claude can do Gmail / Google account Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive Search and read email, draft, reply and send (asks first); view, create and change events; find free slots; search, read and save Drive files Google account Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Slides Edit a file live in a pane next to the chat, create new ones, work with Docs comments and suggestions UB Microsoft 365 (Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams) Microsoft 365 Search email, calendar, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams. Since July 2026 it can also draft and send email, manage events and edit OneDrive/SharePoint files, but only once the administrator has enabled these write tools

Microsoft 365 needs UB IT

The Microsoft 365 connector only works with a work account, once a Microsoft administrator of the organisation has approved it once (write tools need a second approval). Personal accounts such as @outlook.com are not supported. If it says approval is required for your UB account, contact UB IT; until then, use the Gmail connector for a Google account, or forward the relevant emails and upload attachments by hand.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. In a chat, click +, then Connectors (or go to Customize → Connectors).
  2. Click Connect next to Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Google Docs/Sheets/Slides or Microsoft 365.
  3. Sign in with the account you want Claude to use and approve the access.
  4. In each chat, use + to switch connectors on or off. Leave on only what that chat needs.

docs.title: Things to ask
docs.text:
Email

  • "Find all emails from the SOC of the conference in Lisbon and list what they ask me to do, with deadlines."
  • "Summarise the thread about the new GPU node and tell me who is waiting for an answer from me."
  • "Draft a polite reply declining the referee request, suggesting Dr. X instead. Don't send it."

Calendar

  • "What does my week look like? Flag anything that clashes with my Tuesday and Thursday classes."
  • "Find three 1-hour slots in the next two weeks where Anna, Marc and I are all free." (works if their calendars are shared with you)
  • "Create an event on Friday 15:00 to 16:00, 'Group meeting', room 503, and add the agenda from my last email to Pau."

Combined

  • "Every Friday at 16:00, list the emails from this week that are still waiting for an answer from me." (a scheduled task)
  • "I'm back from the conference in Lisbon. Find the registration receipt, flight and hotel confirmations in my email, list the amounts and dates, and draft the reimbursement email to the department administration." See the full example: Conference trip reimbursement.

docs.title: Claude inside Office: the Microsoft 365 add-ins
docs.text:
Separately from the connector, Claude for Microsoft 365 puts Claude in a side panel inside Excel, Word and PowerPoint (and Outlook, in beta). Install them from claude.com/claude-for-microsoft-365 and sign in with your Claude account.

  • Excel: ask about cells and formulas, update a model without breaking it.
  • Word: edits appear as tracked changes; Claude can answer comment threads. Handy for co-written proposals.
  • PowerPoint: build or edit slides in your own template.
  • Outlook (beta): triage your inbox and draft replies that wait for you to send them.

At UB, installing Office add-ins may also need UB IT approval.

docs.title: Keep it safe
docs.text:
• Claude asks before sending, deleting or creating anything. Read what it proposes before you approve. Better: ask for drafts and send them yourself.
  • Your mailbox contains other people's personal data. Ask about specific threads or senders rather than "search all my email", and don't paste the results anywhere public.
  • Emails can contain text written to manipulate AI assistants. Don't let Claude act automatically on instructions found inside an email.
  • Disconnect services you no longer use: Customize → Connectors → Disconnect.

See also Data and privacy.

docs.title: Uploading files
docs.text: Drag files into the chat, or click + next to the message box. Claude then reads them as part of the conversation.

docs.title: What you can upload
docs.text:
Type Formats What Claude sees Documents PDF, DOCX, TXT, RTF, ODT, HTML, EPUB Text. For PDFs under 100 pages, also figures, plots and tables. Data CSV, JSON, XLSX The content. With code execution on, Claude can also analyse it with Python. Code .py, .ipynb, .c, .f90, .tex and other text files The text Images PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP The image: plots, photos of a whiteboard, screenshots, handwritten notes

Limits in a chat: up to 500 MB per file and 20 files per chat. PDFs can have up to 1000 pages; figures are only read in PDFs of 100 pages or fewer. Files you add to a Project are limited to 30 MB each. Images work best at 1000 px or more on a side.

In the desktop app you can also give Claude a whole folder on your computer instead of uploading files one by one. See Longer tasks and scheduling.

Before you upload

Check Data and privacy. No referee reports, no student data with names, no collaboration-internal material unless you have checked the rules.

docs.title: Papers
docs.text:
• "Summarise the method and list the main assumptions."
  • "What do they use for the halo mass function, and how does it differ from Tinker et al.?" (upload both papers)
  • "Explain Figure 4 to a master's student."
  • "Write a 150-word summary for our group journal club announcement."

Claude reads the figures in a PDF, so you can ask about plots directly. Check anything you plan to quote: Claude can misread a number from a plot.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
With Create and edit files (formerly Code execution and file creation) turned on in Settings → Capabilities, Claude can run Python on an uploaded CSV or Excel file: compute statistics, fit a model, make a plot, and give you the resulting file. It can also hand you a spreadsheet with working formulas, a Word document or a PowerPoint deck.

  • "Plot column flux against mjd, with error bars from flux_err, and mark points with flag == 1 in red."
  • "Fit a power law to this spectrum between 1 and 10 keV and give me the index with an uncertainty."

Ask for the code too, so you can rerun and check it on your own machine.

docs.title: Images and screenshots
docs.text:
• A photo of a whiteboard: "Turn this into LaTeX."
  • A plot from a colleague: "What is wrong with this figure for a paper?"
  • A screenshot of an error message: "What does this mean and how do I fix it?"

docs.title: Files you use again and again
docs.text: If you keep uploading the same syllabus, paper or style guide, put it in a Project instead. Every chat in the Project sees it, and it uses less of your allowance than re-uploading.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text: A Project is a folder for chats that share the same files and instructions. Use one per course, paper, proposal or long task.

docs.title: Why use one
docs.text:
• Files once: upload the syllabus, the draft or the data description once; every chat in the Project can use it.
  • Instructions once: tell Claude the audience, style and rules once, not in every chat.
  • Tidy history: all chats about one topic in one place.

Pro gives you as many Projects as you want. Large Projects are handled automatically: Claude searches the Project's files and pulls in the relevant parts.

docs.title: Create one
docs.text:
1. Click Projects in the left sidebar, then + New project.
  2. Give it a name and, optionally, a description.
  3. Add files under Project knowledge: PDFs, text, code, notes.
  4. Click Set project instructions and write them (see below).
  5. Start a chat inside the Project.

docs.title: Write good instructions
docs.text:
Instructions are added to every chat in the Project. Keep them short and concrete.

This Project is for the course "Astrofísica Extragalàctica" (4th year,
Grau en Física, UB). Students know undergraduate physics and basic Python.
- Write course material in Catalan unless I ask otherwise.
- Use the notation from the attached lecture notes.
- Exercises: give a statement, then a full solution in a separate section.
- Never invent references. If you cite something, say whether you are sure it exists.

docs.title: Ideas for ICCUB
docs.text: Project What to put in it A course Syllabus, lecture notes, past exams, notation conventions A paper in progress Your draft, key references, the collaboration's style rules (if sharing is allowed) A grant proposal The call text, evaluation criteria, your CV, previous proposals Your group's code README, a description of the pipeline, coding conventions Outreach Your target audience, past talks, the venue's format

docs.title: Project memory
docs.text:
Each Project has its own memory: what Claude learns in that Project's chats stays there and is not used in other Projects. Inside a Project, Claude also uses your general memory. For a confidential Project (a proposal you are evaluating, a paper under embargo), turn off Use account memory on the Project page so nothing flows in or out.

Chats in the same Project don't see each other's content unless it is in the Project files.

Note

On a Pro plan, Projects are private to you. You cannot share a Project with a colleague; share the files and the instructions instead.

docs.title: Chat and prompting
docs.text: Most of what you will do with Claude is an ordinary chat. A few habits make a big difference.

docs.title: Give context
docs.text:
Claude knows physics and Python, but not you, your project or your audience. Say:

  • Who you are and who the output is for.
  • What the task is, and what you will do with the result.
  • What good looks like: length, format, level, language.
Instead of Try Explain dark matter. I give a 20-minute talk to high-school students next week. Explain the evidence for dark matter in five slides' worth of bullet points, no equations, with one everyday analogy. Fix my code. This function should return the luminosity distance in Mpc for a flat ΛCDM cosmology, but gives values 10% too high at z = 1. Find the bug. (then paste the code) Write an email to students. Write a short, friendly email in Catalan to my Física Quàntica students saying the exam moves from 12 to 19 January, same room.

Instructions you set in Settings → Your Claude are added to every chat, so you don't need to repeat who you are each time (see Your first 30 minutes).

docs.title: Iterate, don't restart
docs.text:
The first answer is a draft. Reply with what to change: "shorter", "more formal", "use numpy instead of loops", "the second point is wrong because…". Claude keeps the whole conversation in mind.

Start a new chat when you change topic. Very long chats get slower, use more of your allowance, and Claude can lose track of early details.

docs.title: Show an example
docs.text: If you want a specific format, paste one. "Format the references like this: …" or "Write the exercise in the same style as this one: …" works better than describing the style.

docs.title: Ask Claude to check its work
docs.text:
• "Check this derivation step by step and tell me where you are least sure."
  • "List any assumptions you made."
  • "Which of these references are you certain exist?"

Claude will often catch its own mistakes when asked. It will not catch all of them: you still have to verify numbers, derivations and citations. See Tips and pitfalls.

docs.title: Useful tricks
docs.text:
• Effort (model menu below the message box; Extended thinking in older versions): raise it for derivations, debugging and anything where a careful answer matters more than a fast one.
  • Edit your message: hover over a message you sent and click the pencil to change it and get a new answer, instead of adding a correction. This starts a new branch; the original answer is kept.
  • Edit part of a draft: when Claude writes a draft (a document, an email, a section), select the passage you want changed and ask for the edit there. Claude only rewrites that part.
  • Hand over the whole task: for bigger jobs (a report, a slide deck, a table from several papers), say what you want at the end and let Claude work through it. See Longer tasks and scheduling.
  • Retry: the retry button under an answer gives you a different version.
  • Ask for questions first: "Before you start, ask me anything you need to know." is useful for bigger tasks like a course outline or a proposal section.
  • Language: Claude works well in English, Spanish and Catalan. Ask in one language and request the answer in another if you need to.

docs.title: Web search and Research
docs.text: By default Claude answers from what it learned in training, which stops at a cut-off date and has no live information. Two features let it look things up.

docs.title: Web search
docs.text:
Claude searches the web during the chat and cites the pages it used.

  • In the current version there is no switch: Claude searches when it helps. You can also ask: "Search the web for…".
  • In the older layout, turn it on with + → Web search.

Good for: recent news, deadlines and calls, software documentation, checking that a paper or dataset exists, finding the current version of a package.

docs.title: Research
docs.text:
Research is a longer investigation. Claude runs many searches, follows leads, and writes a structured report with citations. It usually takes a few minutes.

  • Start it with + → Research, or type /deep-research followed by your question.
  • Write a clear question, with scope: "What X-ray telescopes are planned to launch between 2027 and 2035, what are their energy ranges and effective areas, and which are relevant for galaxy cluster studies?"
  • Research uses more of your allowance than a normal chat. Use it for questions where a report saves you an afternoon.

Good for: a first overview of a field you are entering, comparing software or instruments, background for a proposal, finding funding calls.

docs.title: Check the sources
docs.text:
Web search and Research make invented references much less likely, but not impossible, and a real source can still be misread.

  • Click the citations for anything you will reuse. Check the claim is actually in the source.
  • Prefer primary sources: ask for ADS, arXiv or journal links rather than blogs.
  • Research is not a literature review. It searches the open web and misses paywalled papers and much of the specialist literature. Use it as a starting map, then go to ADS.

See also Tips and pitfalls.

docs.title: Claude Science
docs.text:
Claude Science is Anthropic's desktop app for scientific research, in beta since June 2026 and included in Pro. You describe an analysis in plain language; Claude writes and runs the code in a sandbox, reads the folders you give it, can connect to scientific databases and to your own compute, and saves every result with a record of how it was produced.

Mostly built for the life sciences, for now

Its curated skills and database connectors are aimed at biology and chemistry (genomics, proteins, PubMed…). There is nothing physics- or astronomy-specific yet, such as ADS or astropy-aware tools. For most ICCUB work, Claude Code in a terminal or VS Code is the more mature choice. Claude Science is worth a try if you want its provenance records or its job submission to a cluster.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Download it from the Claude Science page. It runs on macOS 13 or later, Windows 11 (x64) and Linux x64.
  2. Sign in with your Claude Pro account.

If you are on a group's Team plan for scientists, it is switched on by default. On other Team plans, the plan owner enables it.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Runs analyses end to end: writes and runs Python in a sandbox, on files in a folder you provide.
  • Keeps the provenance: each figure or table is saved with its code, environment and conversation, so you (or a referee) can reproduce it later, and ask for edits in plain language.
  • Uses your compute: it drafts a plan, asks before using new resources, and can submit jobs to an HPC cluster over SSH.
  • Checks its own work: a reviewer agent looks at citations and calculations and flags errors. Still check them yourself.
  • Forks a session so you can compare two approaches.

docs.title: Ideas for ICCUB
docs.text:
• "Load the light curves in data/, fit a damped random walk to each, and make a table of the best-fit timescales with uncertainties."
  • "Reproduce Figure 3 of the attached paper from the public catalogue, and tell me where our result differs."
  • "Prepare and submit a job array on our cluster that runs run_mcmc.py for each of the 20 parameter files, then collect the chains when they finish."

docs.title: Stay in control
docs.text:
• Point it at a copy of your data, or a folder you are allowed to share. Data stays on your machine or cluster, but the parts needed for each step are sent to Claude. See Data and privacy.
  • Read the plan before it uses cluster time.
  • It is a beta: expect rough edges and check results as you would a student's first analysis.

Reference: Get started with Claude Science (Anthropic help center).

docs.title: Longer tasks and scheduling
docs.text:
Claude no longer only answers questions. In the same conversation, you can hand it a bigger piece of work (a report, a spreadsheet, a slide deck, a literature table) and it plans the steps, works through them, and gives you finished files. This used to be a separate mode called Cowork; since September 2026 it is part of every chat on Pro, rolling out gradually.

Do you have it yet?

If your message box still shows separate Chat and Cowork options, your account has the older layout. Everything below still works, in the Cowork mode.

docs.title: Hand over a task
docs.text:
Describe the result you want, the material to use and what good looks like, as you would to a colleague:

  • "Using the three attached papers, make a table comparing their samples, methods and constraints on σ8, then write a one-page summary for our group meeting as a Word document."
  • "Read the CSV of last semester's exam marks (anonymised), compute the distribution per question and make five slides on which questions worked and which did not."
  • "Go through the PDFs in my 'Referee guidelines' folder and draft a checklist I can reuse."

Claude may ask a few questions first, then work for several minutes. You can:

  • Watch, stop or redirect it at any time.
  • Run several tasks in parallel in different conversations.
  • Close the laptop: tasks started on the web or mobile keep running in the cloud, and the result appears in the conversation. You can check progress and answer questions from the mobile app.

The results come back as real files: Word documents, spreadsheets with working formulas, PowerPoint-compatible decks, PDFs, or Artifacts (Docs, Slides, Design).

docs.title: How independently Claude works
docs.text:
The permission control in the message box decides whether Claude asks before each step:

Setting What happens Auto (default on Pro) Claude proceeds without asking at each step; automatic safety checks run before actions. Manual Claude asks before each action.

Recommended while you learn

Switch to Manual for anything that touches your email, calendar, files or websites where you are logged in. Read what Claude proposes before you approve.

docs.title: Files on your computer (desktop app)
docs.text:
In the desktop app, you can give Claude access to a folder so it can read, organise and create files there. Set this up under Settings (look for Storage folder and Trusted folders). By default Claude asks before permanently deleting anything.

  • Only grant folders you would be happy to share. Not your whole home directory, not folders with student data or collaboration-internal material. See Data and privacy.
  • Local folders, the built-in browser and computer use only work while the desktop app is open.
  • Computer use (beta on Pro): Claude can click, type and move between apps on your screen. Powerful but slow and risky; keep it for tasks where nothing else works.

docs.title: Scheduled tasks
docs.text:
Ask Claude to repeat a task on a schedule: "Every Monday at 8:00, summarise the new arXiv astro-ph.CO papers that mention weak lensing and email me the list." Scheduled tasks run in the cloud, so they continue when your computer is off. See the weekly arXiv digest example.

Each run uses your allowance. Check your scheduled tasks now and then and delete the ones you no longer need.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
A skill is a set of instructions (and sometimes scripts) that teaches Claude how you want a type of task done. Claude uses a skill automatically when the task comes up.

  • Built-in skills create and edit Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files. They are on by default.
  • Your own skills: for example "how I format exercise sheets for my course" or "the ICCUB template for seminar announcements". Ask Claude in a chat to turn a workflow you just did into a skill, or upload one.
  • Manage them in Customize → Skills. Skills need Create and edit files (formerly Code execution and file creation) switched on in Settings → Capabilities.
  • Plugins bundle skills and connectors for a role. Browse them in the directory under Customize. Only install plugins and skills from sources you trust: they contain instructions Claude will follow.

Sharing skills with colleagues is only possible on Team plans. On Pro, share the skill file itself.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Long tasks use much more of your allowance than a quick question. Check Settings → Usage, and see Usage limits.

docs.title: Current limits
docs.text:
• Incognito chats open in the older experience: Claude cannot create files or run code in them.
  • Old Cowork tasks are in Recents but not in chat search.

Reference: Claude Cowork and chat are one Claude (Anthropic help center).

docs.title: Claude in VS Code
docs.text: Many of us write code, LaTeX and notes in Visual Studio Code. The Claude Code extension puts Claude in a panel inside VS Code, where it can read your project, propose changes as diffs you accept or reject, and run commands. It works with your Pro account; no API key needed.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Open VS Code (version 1.94 or later).
  2. Open the Extensions view: Cmd+Shift+X (Mac) or Ctrl+Shift+X (Windows/Linux).
  3. Search for Claude Code (publisher: Anthropic) and click Install.
  4. Click the spark icon that appears at the top right of an open file, or in the left Activity Bar.
  5. Sign in with your Claude Pro account when asked.

If the icon does not appear, run Developer: Reload Window from the Command Palette (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P).

docs.title: Open your project the right way
docs.text: Claude works on the folder you open in VS Code. Open the folder of your paper, course or analysis (File → Open Folder), not a single file. Claude can then read everything in it, and only that.

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text: You want to… Do this Ask about a piece of code Select the lines. Claude sees the selection automatically. Then ask "What does this do?" Point Claude to a file Type @ and the file name: "Compare @fit_spectrum.py with @fit_spectrum_old.py". Option+K / Alt+K inserts the current selection as a reference. Have Claude change code Describe the change. Claude shows each edit as a diff; accept or reject it. Plan before changing anything Type /plan followed by the task. Claude proposes a plan you can edit before it touches any file. Work on several things Open several conversations in separate tabs. Think harder Raise the effort level (from the / menu) for tricky bugs and derivations.

docs.title: Not just code
docs.text:
VS Code + Claude is also a good way to work on LaTeX papers, lecture notes and Markdown:

  • "Fix all LaTeX warnings in main.tex and make the citation style consistent."
  • "Read my % TODO comments in chapter3.tex and address each one."
  • "Turn notes.md into a structured outline for section 2 of the paper."

See the worked examples: Write a conference proceeding and Lecture notes from slides.

docs.title: Tell Claude about your project
docs.text: Put a CLAUDE.md file at the top of the folder: what the project is, how to run it, conventions, what not to touch. Claude reads it at the start of every conversation. Type /init to have Claude draft one. More in Claude Code.

docs.title: Stay in control
docs.text:
• Use git (VS Code has it built in, in the Source Control panel). Commit before a big change so you can undo it.
  • Read the diffs before accepting. Claude can be confidently wrong.
  • Permission mode: Claude now starts in Auto, where a safety classifier reviews most actions instead of asking you. While you learn, click the mode indicator at the bottom of the prompt box and pick Manual, which asks before each change.
  • Don't open folders that contain secrets or data you are not allowed to share. See Data and privacy.

docs.title: Extension or terminal?
docs.text:
The extension and the terminal version (claude in a terminal, see Claude Code) are the same assistant. The extension is easier if you already live in VS Code; the terminal works everywhere, including over SSH on a cluster. Your conversations are shared between them.

Reference: Claude Code in VS Code (Anthropic documentation).

docs.title: Contribueix
docs.text: Tothom a l'ICCUB pot afegir un exemple o millorar una pàgina. Pot ser breu, i els fracassos són tan útils com els èxits.

docs.title: Envia un exemple
docs.text:
1. Descarrega la plantilla: iccub-example-template.md o copia-la des de la pàgina Plantilla d'exemple.
  2. Omple-la amb qualsevol editor de text (VS Code, TextEdit, Bloc de notes…). Substitueix el text entre angles. N'hi ha prou amb deu o quinze minuts.
  3. Envia-la per correu a vmathieu@ub.edu amb el fitxer adjunt. Afegeix-hi captures de pantalla o altres fitxers si són útils.

Els editors la publicaran al web i t'enviaran l'enllaç.

No saps ben bé com escriure-ho?

Demana-ho a Claude: puja la plantilla, descriu en unes quantes frases què vas fer i demana "Omple aquesta plantilla a partir de la meva descripció. Mantén les meves paraules sempre que puguis i pregunta'm tot el que hi falti." Després revisa el resultat abans d'enviar-lo.

docs.title: Millora una pàgina
docs.text:
Has vist un error, un nom de menú desactualitzat o alguna cosa que hi falta? Escriu a vmathieu@ub.edu amb l'enllaç de la pàgina i què cal canviar.

Si fas servir GitHub, també pots obrir una pull request al repositori del web: les pàgines són fitxers Markdown a docs/.

docs.title: Abans d'enviar-ho
docs.text:
• Elimina qualsevol cosa confidencial: resultats no publicats, dades d'estudiants, contrasenyes, adreces IP privades. Consulta Dades i privadesa.
  • Indica si vols que hi consti el teu nom o si prefereixes mantenir l'anonimat.

docs.title: Plantilla d'exemple
docs.text:
Descarrega la plantilla

O copia tot el contingut del quadre següent en un fitxer nou. Substitueix el text entre angles i després envia el fitxer per correu a vmathieu@ub.edu. Consulta Contribueix.

---
tags:
  - <Recerca | Docència | Divulgació | Gestió>
  - <funcionalitat utilitzada, p. ex. Projects, Claude Code>
---

# <Títol breu que digui què vas fer>

| Sobre aquest exemple | |
| --- | --- |
| **Autor/a** | <Nom, o "Anònim"> |
| **Data** | <AAAA-MM-DD> |
| **Àrea** | <p. ex. Cosmologia, Instrumentació> (opcional) |
| **Eines utilitzades** | <Funcionalitats de Claude o altres eines> |
| **Temps estalviat** | <Unes N hores> (opcional) |

## Objectiu

<Dues o tres frases: què volies fer i per què.>

## Què vaig fer

<Els passos, incloent-hi els prompts o les ordres que vas fer servir.>

## Resultat

<Què en va sortir. Afegeix-hi una captura de pantalla o un fitxer si és útil.>

## Què cal vigilar

<Què va fallar, què vas haver de corregir, què faries diferent.>

docs.text:

  • Organitzar un cicle de seminaris: troba dates al calendari, redacta invitacions i anuncis, i fes el seguiment de les respostes.

docs.title: Reemborsament d'un viatge a un congrés a partir del correu electrònic
docs.text:
Exemple il·lustratiu

Aquest exemple l'han escrit els editors del lloc per mostrar el flux de treball. Encara no és una experiència real de l'ICCUB. Si el proves, envia'ns la teva versió i el substituirem.

Sobre aquest exemple Autor/a Editors de la Guia de Claude de l'ICCUB Data 2026-10-06 Àrea Gestió Eines utilitzades Connectors de Gmail i Google Drive (o Microsoft 365), Claude in Chrome (opcional) Temps estalviat Aproximadament una hora per viatge (estimació)

docs.title: Objectiu
docs.text: En tornar d'un congrés, reunir tot el que cal per al reemborsament del viatge: el rebut de la inscripció, els vols, l'hotel, el transport local i les dates per a les dietes. Després, omplir el full de despeses del departament i redactar el correu per a l'administració, sense haver de remenar desenes de correus.

docs.title: Què vaig fer
docs.text:
1. Vaig connectar la bústia una sola vegada (consulta Correu electrònic, calendari i documents) i vaig activar els connectors de correu i de Drive en un xat nou.

  2. Vaig reunir els documents:

    Vaig assistir a un congrés a Lisboa del 29 de juny al 3 de juliol de 2026. Cerca al meu correu el rebut de la inscripció, les reserves de vols, la confirmació de l'hotel i qualsevol altre pagament relacionat amb aquest viatge. Fes una taula: data, concepte, proveïdor, import, moneda, mètode de pagament i un enllaç al correu. Assenyala tot el que falti.

    Va trobar cinc conceptes i va assenyalar que la factura de l'hotel era una confirmació de reserva, no una factura.

  3. Vaig omplir el formulari. Vaig pujar la plantilla de despeses del departament (Excel) i la llista de normes:

    Omple aquest full de despeses amb els conceptes de la taula. Aplica les normes de dietes del document adjunt per als dies de viatge. Converteix els imports que no siguin en euros amb el tipus de canvi de la data del pagament i indica quin tipus has fet servir.

  4. Vaig redactar el correu:

    Redacta un correu en català per a l'administració del departament, adjuntant-hi el full omplert, amb la llista dels rebuts, i preguntant quin és el procediment per a la factura de l'hotel que falta. No l'enviïs.

  5. Ho vaig comprovar tot amb els rebuts, vaig descarregar els adjunts i vaig enviar el correu jo mateix.

  6. (Opcional) Per a la factura de l'hotel, vaig fer servir Claude in Chrome per iniciar sessió al web de reserves de l'hotel i trobar la pàgina de descàrrega de la factura. Vaig fer clic a "descarregar" jo mateix.

docs.title: Resultat
docs.text: Tots els rebuts trobats, un full de despeses omplert i un esborrany de correu, en uns 15 minuts en lloc d'una hora i mitja. Un document que faltava es va detectar abans de fer la sol·licitud i no després.

docs.title: Què cal vigilar
docs.text:
• Imports i dates: comprova cada xifra amb els rebuts. Estem parlant de diners.
  • Rebuts o confirmacions: l'administració normalment necessita factures. Demana a Claude que assenyali la diferència.
  • Adjunts: els connectors poden llegir adjunts, però és possible que les eines d'escriptura no puguin adjuntar fitxers als correus. Adjunta'ls tu mateix.
  • No el deixis enviar. Demana-li esborranys.
  • Dades personals: la teva bústia conté dades d'altres persones. Limita la cerca al viatge en qüestió.
  • Les normes de la UB canvien: dona-li el document de normes vigent en lloc de refiar-te del que "sap".

docs.text:
Exemple il·lustratiu

Aquest exemple l'han escrit els editors del lloc per mostrar el flux de treball. Encara no és una experiència real de l'ICCUB. Si el proves, envia'ns la teva versió i el substituirem.

Sobre aquest exemple Autor/a Editors de la Guia de Claude de l'ICCUB Data 2026-10-06 Àrea Gestió Eines utilitzades Un Project, connectors de Gmail i Google Calendar Temps estalviat Unes quantes hores per trimestre (estimació)

docs.title: Objectiu
docs.text: Organitzar el cicle de seminaris del grup durant el trimestre: convidar ponents, trobar dates, enviar anuncis i mantenir un calendari, amb menys correus d'anada i tornada.

docs.title: Què vaig fer
docs.text:
1. Vaig crear un Project (projecte) "Seminaris 2026–27" amb la llista de possibles ponents, les normes de reserva de sales i els correus d'anunci de l'any passat com a exemples d'estil. Instruccions: "Anuncis en anglès, breus, amb títol, resum, ponent, data, sala 503 i un espai reservat per a l'enllaç de Zoom."

  2. Vaig trobar dates, amb el connector de calendari:

    Troba tots els dimecres a les 12:00 entre el 14 d'octubre i el 16 de desembre en què no tingui res al calendari. Exclou la setmana del 2 de novembre.

  3. Vaig redactar les invitacions, una per ponent, adaptada a cadascun: "Redacta una invitació per a cada ponent de la llista, proposant-li dues de les dates lliures i esmentant el seu article recent a arXiv si el trobes." Les vaig enviar jo mateix després de llegir-les.

  4. Vaig fer el seguiment de les respostes: més endavant, "Revisa el meu correu per veure si hi ha respostes a les invitacions al seminari i actualitza la taula del calendari. Qui no ha respost?"

  5. Vaig crear els esdeveniments al calendari i els anuncis quan un ponent confirmava: "Crea l'esdeveniment al calendari i redacta l'anunci per a la llista de correu de l'ICCUB a partir del títol i el resum que hi ha al seu correu."

docs.title: Resultat
docs.text: El calendari de tot un trimestre organitzat en dues sessions curtes, anuncis coherents i una taula que mostrava a qui calia enviar encara un recordatori.

docs.title: Què cal vigilar
docs.text:
• Comprova la informació dels ponents (afiliació, títol, article) abans que aparegui en un anunci.
  • Accions al calendari: Claude et demana confirmació abans de crear esdeveniments. Llegeix amb atenció la data, l'hora i la zona horària, sobretot amb ponents a distància.
  • Envia tu mateix les invitacions. Una nota personal teva funciona millor que una plantilla perfecta.

docs.text:
• Una pàgina web animada per a un acte públic: una pàgina interactiva de "construeix un sistema solar" per a una jornada de portes obertes, feta com a Artifact i publicada amb un enllaç.
  • Preparar una xerrada divulgativa a partir d'un article de recerca: fil narratiu, analogies, pla de diapositives i preguntes probables per a un públic no especialista.

docs.title: Una pàgina web animada per a un acte públic
docs.text:
Exemple il·lustratiu

Aquest exemple l'han escrit els editors del lloc per mostrar el flux de treball. Encara no és una experiència real de l'ICCUB. Si el proves, envia'ns la teva versió i el substituirem.

Sobre aquest exemple Autor/a Editors de la Guia de Claude de l'ICCUB Data 2026-10-06 Àrea Divulgació Eines utilitzades Artifacts de claude.ai i, després, Claude Code per a la versió final Temps estalviat Dies de desenvolupament web, per a algú que no fa llocs web (estimació)

docs.title: Objectiu
docs.text: Per a l'estand d'una jornada de portes obertes, fer una pàgina interactiva amb què els visitants puguin jugar en una tauleta: "Construeix un sistema solar", on col·loques planetes al voltant d'una estrella i en veus les òrbites, amb una breu explicació de les lleis de Kepler. Sense necessitat de saber desenvolupament web.

docs.title: Què vaig fer
docs.text:
1. Ho vaig descriure en un xat, demanant un Artifact (artefacte):

    Fes una pàgina web interactiva per a una fira de ciència, per a visitants a partir de 10 anys. Una estrella al centre; els visitants toquen la pantalla per afegir planetes a diferents distàncies; els planetes orbiten amb velocitats realistes segons Kepler (els interiors, més ràpid). Mostra el període orbital de cada planeta. Un botó "Explica" obre una explicació de tres frases de la tercera llei de Kepler. Botons grans, que funcioni en una tauleta, amb colors vius però no infantil. Text en català, castellà i anglès amb un selector d'idioma.

  2. Vaig iterar jugant-hi, en el mateix xat:

    Els planetes són massa petits en una tauleta. Afegeix estela darrere dels planetes. Afegeix un botó de "reinicia". Quan dos planetes siguin massa a prop, mostra un avís "Òrbita inestable!".

  3. Vaig comprovar la física: "Mostra'm la fórmula que fas servir per al període i les unitats." Vaig verificar que, en doblar la distància, el període es multiplica per 2,83.

  4. El vaig publicar amb el botó Publish de l'Artifact per obtenir un enllaç i un codi QR per a l'estand. Per tenir-ne una versió permanent al web de l'ICCUB, vaig descarregar el fitxer HTML i el vaig passar a l'equip web.

docs.title: Resultat
docs.text: Una pàgina funcional, bilingüe i adaptada a pantalles tàctils en aproximadament una hora, utilitzada en una tauleta a l'estand. Els nens hi jugaven; els pares llegien l'explicació.

docs.title: Què cal vigilar
docs.text:
• Dreceres en la física: les animacions sovint falsegen la física (òrbites circulars, proporcions de velocitat incorrectes). Pregunta què es calcula i comprova-ho.
  • Traduccions: fes que un parlant nadiu revisi els textos en català i en castellà.
  • Els Artifacts publicats són públics: qualsevol persona amb l'enllaç els pot veure. No hi posis res confidencial.
  • Prova-ho al dispositiu real abans de l'acte: les tauletes tenen mides de pantalla i comportaments tàctils diferents.
  • Per a una cosa més gran (diverses pàgines, mantingudes durant anys), fes servir Claude Code en un repositori com cal en lloc d'un Artifact.

docs.title: Preparar una xerrada divulgativa a partir d'un article de recerca
docs.text:
Exemple il·lustratiu

Aquest exemple l'han escrit els editors del lloc per mostrar el flux de treball. Encara no és una experiència real de l'ICCUB. Si el proves, envia'ns la teva versió i el substituirem.

Sobre aquest exemple Autor/a Editors de la Guia de Claude de l'ICCUB Data 2026-10-06 Àrea Divulgació Eines utilitzades Xat de claude.ai amb pujada de fitxers, Artifacts Temps estalviat Aproximadament mig dia (estimació)

docs.title: Objectiu
docs.text: Fer una xerrada de 30 minuts en un centre cultural (a l'estil de "Pint of Science") sobre el nostre article recent sobre ones gravitacionals, per a un públic adult sense formació científica.

docs.title: Què vaig fer
docs.text:
1. Vaig pujar l'article i vaig descriure el públic:

    Faré una xerrada de 30 minuts sobre aquest article per a adults sense formació científica, en un bar, en català. Proposa'm un fil narratiu: un ganxo inicial, tres idees clau com a màxim i un final que la gent recordi. Sense equacions.

  2. Vaig demanar analogies i les vaig comprovar:

    Dona'm cinc analogies quotidianes de com funciona un detector d'ones gravitacionals. Per a cadascuna, digues on deixa de funcionar l'analogia.

    En vaig quedar dues; vaig descartar les que induïen a error.

  3. Vaig construir el pla de diapositives: "Converteix el fil narratiu en 15 diapositives: títol, una frase de text com a màxim i quina imatge s'hi ha de mostrar." Vaig fer les diapositives jo mateix amb el programari habitual i amb imatges reals (imatges públiques de l'ESA, la NASA i LIGO, amb els crèdits).

  4. Em vaig preparar per a les preguntes: "Quines són les deu preguntes que és més probable que faci una persona curiosa no especialista després d'aquesta xerrada? Redacta una resposta breu i honesta per a cadascuna."

  5. Vaig assajar enganxant el guió del que diria i preguntant: "On es perdria una persona no especialista? Quines frases són massa llargues per dir-les en veu alta?"

docs.title: Resultat
docs.text: Un fil narratiu clar, un pla de diapositives, dues bones analogies i una llista de preguntes probables. La xerrada en si, les imatges i la manera d'explicar-ho van continuar sent meves.

docs.title: Què cal vigilar
docs.text:
• Les analogies poden induir a error. Pregunta sempre on deixen de funcionar.
  • Simplificació o error: comprova que les afirmacions simplificades continuen sent certes.
  • Imatges: Claude no et pot proporcionar imatges utilitzables; fes servir imatges públiques d'agències, amb els crèdits, o imatges pròpies.
  • Que no soni genèric. Afegeix-hi les teves pròpies històries: per què treballes en això, què et va sorprendre.

docs.title: Exemples de recerca
docs.text:
• Escriure uns proceedings d'un congrés: les diapositives, la nota d'anàlisi i la plantilla del congrés en una sola carpeta, un prompt llarg i uns proceedings acabats en una mitja hora.
  • Accelerar el codi d'un article publicat: codi de Monte Carlo escrit a mà revisat per Claude, Antigravity i un model local, ara més de 10 vegades més ràpid.
  • Executar un LLM local al teu portàtil: instal·la Ollama, tria un model que càpiga a la teva RAM i fes-lo servir des del terminal i des de VS Code.
  • Compartir un LLM local a través de la xarxa: serveix models des d'un Mac a un altre a la mateixa xarxa, incloent-hi un agent de programació funcional a VS Code.
  • Un resum setmanal d'arXiv: una tasca programada que cada dilluns al matí busca a INSPIRE els articles nous que citen la teva feina i els dels teus temes.

docs.title: Accelerar el codi d'un article publicat
docs.text: Sobre aquest exemple Autor/a Vincent Mathieu Data 2026-10-09 Àrea Física hadrònica (teoria) Eines utilitzades Claude Code, Google Antigravity (Gemini) i un model local, cadascun amb accés a la carpeta del codi Temps estalviat Revisió feta en una mitja hora; ara el codi és més de 10 vegades més ràpid Article High-energy η(′)π photoproduction and the nature of exotic waves, G. Montaña, V. Mathieu et al., Phys. Lett. B 872 (2026) 140101 (arXiv:2510.14549)

docs.title: Objectiu
docs.text:
El 2025 vam publicar un article amb la Gloria Montaña i altres col·legues sobre la producció d'ηπ a alta energia. El model té cinc variables, i calcular els observables volia dir integrar sobre quatre d'elles.

Vaig escriure el codi de Monte Carlo jo mateix, força de pressa, en part mentre viatjava. Vaig decidir no fer servir cap llibreria: volia entendre cada pas, així que totes les rutines estaven escrites a mà, des de la integració de Monte Carlo fins al determinant d'una matriu 6×6 que serveix per comprovar els límits de la regió física. Funcionava, i es va fer servir per a l'article, però un càlcul complet trigava hores.

Un any després, quan vaig començar a fer servir eines de programació amb IA, vaig voler saber si aquest codi es podia fer més ràpid.

docs.title: Què vaig fer
docs.text:
1. Vaig donar a l'eina accés a la carpeta amb el codi que havia produït els resultats publicats.
  2. Vaig explicar el context: l'article, i que aquest era el codi que s'hi havia fet servir.
  3. Vaig demanar una revisió, en essència: "Aquest és el codi que es va fer servir per publicar aquest article. Revisa tots els fitxers i mira si el podem optimitzar."
  4. Vaig repetir l'exercici amb tres eines: Google Antigravity (amb Gemini), Claude (Sonnet, a Claude Code) i un model local, per veure si arribaven a les mateixes conclusions.

docs.title: Resultat
docs.text:
La revisió va durar una mitja hora. Va trobar:

  • Feina duplicada: diversos llocs on es calculava la mateixa quantitat dues vegades, cadascun un factor 2.
  • Rutines poc eficients: la meva rutina feta a mà per al determinant no era eficient.

Tot plegat va donar una acceleració de més d'un factor 10. Un any després de l'article, el mateix codi va molt, molt més ràpid.

Les tres eines (Antigravity, Claude i el model local) van portar a la mateixa conclusió: el codi va ser molt més eficient després de la revisió amb IA.

docs.title: Què cal vigilar
docs.text:
• Escriu-lo tu primer. Crec que és bona idea començar programant cada funció tu mateix, sense llibreries, per entendre tant la física com el codi.
  • Després optimitza amb IA. Quan el codi funciona i està comprovat, i el necessites eficient per produir els resultats definitius, demana a una IA que l'optimitzi. Mantens la comprensió i tens un codi eficient.
  • Comprova que els resultats no canvien. Compara la sortida del codi optimitzat amb els resultats publicats abans de fer-lo servir.
  • Qualsevol eina serveix. Aquí una eina al núvol i un model local van trobar les mateixes millores; si el teu codi no pot sortir de la teva màquina, consulta Executar un LLM local al teu portàtil.

docs.title: Escriure uns proceedings d'un congrés
docs.text: Sobre aquest exemple Autor/a Vincent Mathieu Data 2026-09-28 Àrea Física hadrònica (teoria) Eines utilitzades Claude amb accés a una carpeta local del projecte Temps estalviat Els proceedings es van escriure en una mitja hora Resultat Meson photoproduction at Jefferson Lab: from two-meson final states to meson-baryon spin-density matrices (INSPIRE)

docs.title: Objectiu
docs.text:
Dos mesos abans havia fet una xerrada plenària al congrés MESON a Cracòvia. Normalment no escric proceedings, però aquesta vegada els meus col·legues experimentals de la col·laboració GlueX en necessitaven. Havien fet servir fórmules que jo havia derivat i que encara no estan publicades, perquè l'article no està acabat. Un estudiant de doctorat que havia fet l'anàlisi volia presentar els seus resultats preliminars en uns proceedings propis, i necessitava una referència per al formalisme. Així que em van demanar que escrivís uns proceedings que poguessin citar.

La petició em va arribar per Slack mentre era en un altre congrés, escoltant xerrades. No tenia temps d'escriure'ls jo mateix.

docs.title: Què vaig fer
docs.text:
1. Vaig crear una carpeta nova per als proceedings i hi vaig posar:

    • les diapositives de la meva xerrada al MESON,
    • la meva nota d'anàlisi, la que faré servir més endavant per escriure l'article complet,
    • la plantilla de LaTeX descarregada del web del congrés.

  2. Vaig donar accés a Claude a tot el que hi havia a la carpeta.

  3. Vaig escriure un prompt llarg explicant a Claude tota la història:

    • Vaig fer una xerrada plenària en aquest congrés, amb l'enllaç al web del congrés.
    • Les diapositives són el contingut de la xerrada, i la nota d'anàlisi conté el formalisme.
    • Per què calen els proceedings: els meus col·legues de GlueX i el seu estudiant de doctorat han de poder citar el formalisme abans que surti l'article.
    • Els proceedings han de seguir la plantilla del congrés.

  4. Vaig llegir l'esborrany. Al cap d'una mitja hora els proceedings ja estaven escrits.

  5. Els vaig acabar a mà:

    • vaig treure una frase que no era adequada,
    • vaig afegir el meu correu electrònic i els números dels meus projectes de finançament,
    • els vaig enviar a arXiv i a les actes del congrés.

docs.title: Resultat
docs.text:
Els proceedings eren clars, concisos, exactament el que volia, i amb el format que demanava el congrés. Llevat de la frase que vaig treure, vaig mantenir el text tal com l'havia escrit Claude.

Són a arXiv i a INSPIRE: Meson photoproduction at Jefferson Lab: from two-meson final states to meson-baryon spin-density matrices. Ara els meus col·legues poden citar el formalisme en els seus propis proceedings.

docs.title: Què cal vigilar
docs.text:
• Dona tot el context. El prompt llarg amb tota la història (qui ho necessita, per què i què ha de contenir) és el que va fer que el primer esborrany fos aprofitable.
  • Posa les fonts reals a la carpeta. Les diapositives, la nota d'anàlisi i la plantilla oficial van fer que Claude treballés a partir del meu material i no de coneixement general.
  • Llegeix cada frase. Una frase no era adequada i vaig haver de treure-la. L'autor continues sent tu.
  • Treball no publicat. La nota d'anàlisi contenia resultats que encara no estan publicats. Comprova què pots compartir abans de donar-hi accés a Claude. Consulta Dades i privadesa.
  • Els detalls els has d'afegir tu: correu electrònic de l'autor, afiliacions, números de projectes de finançament, agraïments.

docs.title: Executar un LLM local al teu portàtil
docs.text: Sobre aquest exemple Autor/a Vincent Mathieu Data per confirmar Eines utilitzades Ollama, Gemma 2, Hermes Agent, VS Code amb l'extensió Continue Per què en local Les dades no surten mai de la teva màquina, sense cost per tokens, funciona sense connexió

docs.title: Objectiu
docs.text: Executar un model de llenguatge de pesos oberts completament en un portàtil personal, fer-lo servir com a assistent de xat al terminal i connectar-lo a VS Code com a assistent de programació, de manera que el codi i les dades sensibles no vagin mai a un servei al núvol.

docs.title: 1. Tria un model que càpiga a la teva RAM
docs.text:
Els models de pesos oberts tenen mides que es mesuren en milers de milions de paràmetres (2B, 8B, 27B). Normalment es distribueixen quantitzats a 4 bits (Q4), cosa que redueix molt la memòria necessària amb poca pèrdua de qualitat.

RAM del portàtil Models recomanats Ordre Útil per a 8 GB Gemma 2 2B, Phi-3 Mini 3.8B ollama run gemma2:2b Xat ràpid, fragments de codi, redacció sense connexió 16 GB Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B ollama run gemma2:9b El punt òptim: raonament, ajuda amb el codi, anàlisi 32 GB o més Gemma 2 27B, Qwen 2.5 14B o 32B ollama run gemma2:27b Raonament més difícil, refactoritzacions més grans, tasques d'agent

docs.title: 2. Instal·la Ollama
docs.text:
Ollama s'executa en segon pla, descarrega models i els serveix a través d'una API local a http://localhost:11434.

  • macOS: descarrega'l des de ollama.com/download, o brew install ollama
  • Windows: descarrega i executa OllamaSetup.exe des de ollama.com/download
  • Linux: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

Ordres essencials:

ollama run gemma2:9b   # download the model if needed and start a chat
ollama list            # models stored on this machine
ollama ps              # model currently loaded in memory
ollama rm gemma2:9b    # delete a model to free disk space

docs.title: 3. Opcional: un agent de terminal (Hermes Agent)
docs.text:
ollama run ofereix un simple xatbot. Un entorn d'agent com Hermes Agent converteix el terminal en un espai de treball on el model pot llegir i executar fitxers i cridar eines.

  1. En el primer inici, Hermes et pregunta quin backend d'inferència vols fer servir: tria Ollama.
  2. Detecta els models que has descarregat (per exemple gemma2:9b) a localhost:11434.
hermes agent --model gemma2:9b

docs.title: 4. VS Code amb l'extensió Continue
docs.text:
1. Obre la pestanya d'extensions (Cmd+Shift+X o Ctrl+Shift+X).
  2. Instal·la Continue.
  3. Continue detecta Ollama a localhost:11434 i mostra la llista dels teus models. Per fixar-ne un explícitament, afegeix a la seva configuració:
{ "models": [ { "title": "Local Gemma 2 (9B)", "provider": "ollama", "model": "gemma2:9b" } ] }

Dreceres: Cmd+L / Ctrl+L obre el xat sobre els fitxers que tens oberts; Cmd+I / Ctrl+I edita el codi seleccionat en línia; Tab accepta les compleccions.

docs.title: Resultat
docs.text:
Un assistent local que funciona al terminal i a VS Code. Dues proves ràpides que van funcionar:

  • Al terminal: ollama run gemma2:9b, i després "Escriu una funció de Python que validi adreces de correu electrònic amb una expressió regular."
  • A VS Code: selecciona un bloc de codi, prem Cmd+I i demana "Afegeix docstrings i anotacions de tipus, i gestiona el possible ZeroDivisionError." Revisa el diff i després accepta'l.

docs.title: Què cal vigilar
docs.text:
• Soroll del ventilador o respostes lentes: executa ollama ps. En màquines de 8 o 16 GB, assegura't que només hi ha un model gran carregat. Ollama descarrega de la memòria els models inactius al cap d'uns 5 minuts.
  • Qualitat: els models locals petits queden molt per darrere de Claude en raonament difícil. Fes-los servir quan la privadesa o l'ús sense connexió siguin importants, no com a substitut directe.

Pas següent: comparteix els models d'una màquina amb els col·legues a través de la xarxa.

docs.title: Compartir un LLM local a través de la xarxa
docs.text: Sobre aquest exemple Autor/a Vincent Mathieu Data 2026-09-26 Eines utilitzades Ollama, LM Studio, VS Code amb l'extensió Continue Configuració Un MacBook Pro més nou com a servidor, un MacBook Pro més antic com a client, a la mateixa xarxa local

docs.title: Objectiu
docs.text:
Comprovar que els models locals que s'executen en un Mac (el servidor) es poden fer servir des d'un segon Mac (el client) a la mateixa xarxa, tant com a model de xat com a agent de programació a VS Code. És una prova de concepte per a una estació de treball compartida que doni servei a diversos investigadors, sense costos d'API al núvol i sense que cap dada surti de la xarxa local.

Models al servidor: qwen3-coder:30b, qwen2.5-coder:7b, gemma4:e4b, gemma4:e2b, gemma4:12b-mlx.

docs.title: 1. Servidor: exposar Ollama i LM Studio a la xarxa
docs.text:
Troba l'adreça IP del servidor:

ipconfig getifaddr en0

Per defecte, Ollama només escolta a localhost. Fes que escolti a la xarxa:

launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "0.0.0.0:11434"

Tanca Ollama del tot i torna'l a obrir, i després comprova que mostra la llista dels teus models:

curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags

Per a LM Studio: pestanya Developer (Server), carrega un model, inicia el servidor i configura'l perquè serveixi a la xarxa local en lloc de 127.0.0.1. El port per defecte és 1234.

docs.title: 2. Servidor: tallafoc
docs.text: A System Settings, Network, Firewall: si el tallafoc està activat, accepta els avisos de connexió entrant per a Ollama i LM Studio el primer cop que s'hi connecti un client, o afegeix-los a Firewall Options.

docs.title: 3. Client: comprova la connexió i xateja des del terminal
docs.text:
Substitueix <server-ip> per l'adreça del servidor:

ping <server-ip>
curl http://<server-ip>:11434/api/tags
curl http://<server-ip>:1234/v1/models

Xateja amb un model que s'executa al servidor (el client necessita tenir Ollama instal·lat, però cap model):

OLLAMA_HOST=http://<server-ip>:11434 ollama run qwen3-coder:30b

Aquesta va ser la primera prova que l'accés remot funciona.

docs.title: 4. Client: VS Code amb l'extensió Continue
docs.text:
1. Instal·la Continue (l'agent de codi amb IA de codi obert) a VS Code.
  2. Instal·la també l'extensió YAML de Red Hat. Sense aquesta extensió, Continue no aconsegueix llegir la seva configuració i no avisa de l'error.
  3. Fes una còpia de seguretat de qualsevol ~/.continue/config.yaml existent i després escriu:
name: Remote LAN Models
version: 1.0.0
schema: v1

models:
  - name: "Qwen3 Coder 30B (remote)"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3-coder:30b
    apiBase: http://<server-ip>:11434
    roles: [chat, edit, apply]
    capabilities: [tool_use]
    defaultCompletionOptions:
      contextLength: 32768

  - name: "Qwen2.5 Coder 7B (remote, faster)"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen2.5-coder:7b
    apiBase: http://<server-ip>:11434
    roles: [chat, edit, apply]
    capabilities: [tool_use]

  - name: "Gemma4 e4b (remote, general)"
    provider: ollama
    model: gemma4:e4b
    apiBase: http://<server-ip>:11434
    roles: [chat]
  1. Executa Cmd+Shift+P i després Developer: Reload Window.
  2. Obre el panell de Continue, tria un model i envia un missatge de prova.

docs.title: 5. Proves
docs.text:
Des d'una carpeta buida, en el mode Agent de Continue:

  1. Comprovació de la connexió: "Quin model ets i quant fa 17 × 24?"
  2. Ús d'eines: "Crea en aquesta carpeta un fitxer anomenat hello.py que imprimeixi 'Hello from the remote model' i després executa'l."
  3. Edició en diversos passos: "Afegeix a hello.py una funció que calculi la successió de Fibonacci fins a n=10 i torna'l a executar."

docs.title: Resultat
docs.text: Funciona de punta a punta: tant el xat al terminal com el mode Agent de VS Code van funcionar amb el model remot, i el mateix model va crear i executar hello.py. Clarament més lent que executar-lo en local, sobretot amb el model de 30B, però correcte.

docs.title: Què cal vigilar
docs.text:
• El mode Agent mostra les crides a eines en lloc d'executar-les: és un error conegut de Continue amb provider: ollama als modes Agent i Plan (el xat normal funciona bé). Canvia aquest model a provider: openai, amb apiBase: http://<server-ip>:11434/v1 i una apiKey: "ollama" de marcador de posició.
  • La configuració s'ignora sense avisar: instal·la l'extensió YAML de Red Hat.
  • Velocitat: el model de 30B és lent a través de la xarxa. Fes servir el model de 7B quan importi la rapidesa de resposta.
  • Canvis d'adreça IP: assigna al servidor una IP fixa o un nom d'amfitrió .local abans que diverses persones en depenguin, o totes les configuracions dels clients deixaran de funcionar quan canviï l'adreça.

docs.title: Consells per a una demostració
docs.text: Mostra primer el xat al terminal (el més senzill) i després la prova de creació de fitxers a VS Code, que és el moment més convincent d'"agent de programació de veritat". Tria el model de 7B si la demostració ha de semblar ràpida, o explica el compromís: privadesa i cost zero a canvi de velocitat.

docs.title: Un resum setmanal d'arXiv, cada dilluns
docs.text: Sobre aquest exemple Autor/a Vincent Mathieu Data 2026-10-12 Àrea Física hadrònica (teoria) Eines utilitzades Una scheduled task de Claude, l'API pública d'INSPIRE-HEP Temps estalviat La revisió dels articles nous del dilluns, cada setmana

docs.title: Objectiu
docs.text:
Cada setmana surten desenes d'articles a hep-ph, nucl-th i hep-lat. Volia una llista curta el dilluns al matí amb dues coses: els articles nous que citen la meva feina i els articles nous sobre els meus temes (teoria de Regge, fotoproducció, anàlisi d'amplituds, hadrons exòtics, glueballs, regles de suma, espectroscòpia en el reticle), cadascun amb una o dues frases sobre per què m'interessa.
